axes.model_access: The core is an open-source model family: v1 (CosyVoice-300M) → v2 (CosyVoice2-0.5B) → Fun-CosyVoice 3.0 (Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512, the three-generation line on record in the README same day); download the weights and run inference locally, no hosted API.
axes.runtime: Local Python runtime (the README gives conda install + inference/training/deployment full stack, official description "inference, training and deployment full-stack ability"); the repo moved to the QwenAudio org (FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice 301 → QwenAudio/CosyVoice, verified same day); the README's clone command still writes the old org name.
axes.local_files: Weights, code and synthesized output all stay on your machine — an open-source model repo has no account-side data surface (the structural difference from hosted TTS products).
axes.background: Local batch/streaming inference: Bi-Streaming is on record in the README (text-in/audio-out dual streams, official claim of latency as low as 150ms); no cloud task surface.
axes.tools: Pronunciation-control surface on record (README: Chinese Pinyin / English CMU phoneme pronunciation inpainting, text normalization without a traditional frontend, Instruct support for emotion/speed/volume commands); MCP does not apply (a model repo is not an agent host).
axes.context: The conversational-context dimension does not apply — a TTS model works per synthesis request; zero-shot cloning conditions on reference audio (multilingual/cross-lingual zero-shot cloning on record in the README).
axes.permissions: Apache-2.0 code license (GitHub API verified same day); voice cloning touches personality rights — the official README carries no usage-consent clause, labeled as "not declared by the official side" per the pages checked (README/repo root files); 9 languages + 18 Chinese dialects coverage on record in the README.
axes.fit: Fits: local/private Chinese + dialect TTS, zero-shot cloning with a full training/fine-tuning stack, an Apache-2.0 commercial base. Not a fit: out-of-box hosted APIs (the official line sells none), zero-ops setups.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to audio models).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Reproducing the official evaluation table** (the README's eval table is the authors' self-reported numbers — CER/SS not third-party re-checked)
- **Real-time streaming latency on consumer GPUs** (the official 150ms claim is on specific hardware)
- **Minimum reference-audio length/quality for zero-shot cloning** (no hard spec in the README)

related: Same open-source-speech-model-as-repo convention: Whisper handles transcription (listening), CosyVoice handles synthesis (speaking).
Also a zero-shot cloning route: fish audio is a hosted product + voice marketplace, CosyVoice is open weights run locally.
Commercial hosted-TTS contrast: ElevenLabs sells a service, CosyVoice gives weights and the full-stack code.
